subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the equation of the plane passing through the points A(2, 3, −1), B(4, 5, 2) and C(3, 6, 5).

mark_split.label: Find two vectors lying in the plane
Cross them to get the normal
Write the Cartesian equation and check

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.79, chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Long Answer question 8. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1+2+1+1+2 split puts the heaviest weight on the cross product that produces the normal and on the closing Cartesian form, where all three points are checked. Paper position: Maths-1A Section C prints 3 long answers at 8 marks each and the student answers any 2; Product of Vectors is one of the units that can fill a Section-C slot. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the equation of a plane through three given points.

steps.label: Write the position vectors
steps.margin_note: First mark. Turn the three coordinate triples into vectors before anything else. Every later step reads off these three rows.
steps.memory_tip: Turn the three coordinate triples into vectors before anything else.

recall.must_convey: That the three points are written as position vectors a, b and c.
accept: write the three points as position vectors a b and c
convert the coordinate triples into i j k form
turn the three points into vectors first
moodu points ni position vectors ga rasta
a is two i plus three j minus k and so on

steps.why: The cross product works on vectors, not on coordinate triples, so the conversion has to happen first.
common_mistakes: Reading a coordinate in the wrong order.
Missing the minus sign on the third coordinate of A.

steps.label: Find two vectors in the plane
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Both differences start from the same point A. Two vectors from different starting points would still lie in the plane, but starting from A keeps the arithmetic in one place.
steps.memory_tip: Both vectors from the same point A, so the subtractions share one row.

recall.must_convey: That AB = 2i + 2j + 3k and AC = i + 3j + 6k are two vectors lying in the plane, both taken from A.
accept: find AB and AC from the same point A, both lie in the plane
AB is b minus a and AC is c minus a
two i plus two j plus three k, and i plus three j plus six k
A nunchi rendu vectors, avi plane lo untai
build two in plane vectors from one vertex

steps.why: Any two vectors joining points of the plane lie inside it, and two non-parallel ones fix its direction completely.
common_mistakes: Using the position vectors themselves instead of the differences.
Subtracting the wrong way round, which reverses both vectors.

steps.label: Cross them
steps.margin_note: Two marks. The cross product of two vectors that lie in the plane is at right angles to the whole plane. AB goes on the top row, AC below.
steps.memory_tip: The cross of two vectors IN the plane is at right angles to the plane.

lines.text: n = AB \times AC = \begin{vmatrix} i & j & k \\ 2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & 6 \end{vmatrix}

recall.must_convey: That the cross product AB × AC gives a normal to the plane, here 3i − 9j + 4k.
accept: cross AB with AC to get three i minus nine j plus four k
the cross product is at right angles to the plane
the normal is three i minus nine j plus four k
cross product plane ki perpendicular, three minus nine four
expand the determinant to find the normal

steps.why: A cross product is at right angles to both its factors. Since both factors lie in the plane, the result is at right angles to the plane itself.
common_mistakes: Taking a dot product, which gives a number and no direction.
Losing the minus on the j term.

steps.label: Find a · n
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. Any one of the three points can be used here. A is the shortest because its third coordinate is −1.
steps.memory_tip: Any of the three points works. Use the one with the smallest numbers.

recall.must_convey: That a·n = −25, found by dotting any one of the three points with the normal.
accept: dot a with the normal to get minus twenty five
six minus twenty seven minus four is minus twenty five
any of the three points gives the same number
a dot n minus twenty five vasthundi
the constant on the right hand side is minus twenty five

steps.why: Every point of the plane has the same dot product with the normal, so this single number is the constant term of the plane equation.
common_mistakes: Dotting the normal with AB instead of with a position vector, which gives 0.

steps.label: Write the vector equation
steps.margin_note: Fifth mark. The plane is every point r whose dot product with n matches the one A gives. That single line is the vector equation.
steps.memory_tip: The plane is every r with the SAME dot product against n that A has.
lines: The plane is r·n = a·n, that is

recall.must_convey: That the vector equation of the plane is r·(3i − 9j + 4k) = −25.
accept: the vector equation is r dot three i minus nine j plus four k equals minus twenty five
r dot n equals a dot n
every point of the plane has the same dot product with the normal
r dot n equals minus twenty five ani rasta
write the plane in r dot n form

steps.why: Writing r·n = a·n before substituting coordinates keeps the vector form and the Cartesian form clearly separate, and the paper may ask for either.
common_mistakes: Writing r·n = 0, which is the parallel plane through the origin.
Putting the normal on the right and the constant on the left.

steps.label: Write the Cartesian equation
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. Substitute r = xi + yj + zk, then move the −25 across. Checking all three points costs three short lines and catches any earlier slip.
steps.memory_tip: Check all three points, not just one. A wrong normal can still fit a single point.

recall.must_convey: That the Cartesian equation is 3x − 9y + 4z + 25 = 0, and that all three given points satisfy it.
accept: the plane is three x minus nine y plus four z plus twenty five equals zero
substitute r as x i plus y j plus z k to get the Cartesian form
all three points satisfy it, so the answer is right
moodu points ni check cheste zero vasthundi
three x minus nine y plus four z equals minus twenty five

steps.why: One point will fit almost any wrong normal, but all three fitting at once is a real check. It is the cheapest verification available in this question.
common_mistakes: Checking only the point already used to find the constant.
Moving the −25 across without changing its sign.
